# Regionssundhedsdirektørkredsen

Regionssundhedsdirektørkredsen is a Danish health-administrative organization named as a participant in the steering group ("styregruppe") of the ADHD-databasen, a national Danish health database that monitors the quality of assessment and treatment of ADHD in children and young people under 18 years of age [^src1][^src2]. The organization appears in the annual ADHD database reports for both the 2023 and 2024 reporting periods, indicating a continuing role in the governance of the database over time [^src1][^src2].

The broader documents in which Regionssundhedsdirektørkredsen appears describe the steering group's composition as drawing on senior physicians, medical specialists, psychologists, nurses, epidemiologists, and relative/patient representatives from across Denmark [^src1]. In the most recent iteration, the steering group is described as representing all five Danish regions, professional societies, patient organizations, and the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src2]. These reports also present statistical data on children and young people assessed or treated for ADHD, including findings that children and young people with ADHD have a markedly lower rate of passing the lower-secondary school leaving exam (folkeskolens afgangsprøve) before age 17 compared with the background population [^src1], and appendices detailing demographic and regional data on ADHD assessment and treatment pathways, including regional variation in the use of a pathway marker for "disproven suspicions" of ADHD [^src2].

No specific relationships, individual claims, or timeline events tied directly to Regionssundhedsdirektørkredsen are documented beyond its listed presence in the steering group across these two reporting periods.
